label: prop:blowup-yekutieli
title: Blowup mechanism as Yekutieli lifting obstruction in the brane tower
html:
Proposition. Blowup mechanism as Yekutieli lifting obstruction in the brane tower

The regularity breakdown at q = 1 is a cohomological obstruction in the Yekutieli lifting framework.

Brane tower and regularity

The recursive brane tower \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0} with jet prolongations A_n \hookrightarrow A_{n+1} produces a sequence of central extensions of gerbes:

  1 \to \mathcal{B}
  \to \mathfrak{G}_{n+1}
  \to \mathfrak{G}_n
  \to 1.

Each carries an obstruction class \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}) (quantum characteristic classes). A velocity field v on the state bundle \mathcal{S} is smooth if and only if it lifts through the entire tower. It admits a compatible representative at every level A_n:

  v \text{ smooth}
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  \kappa_n(v) = 0  \forall n \geq 0.

Blowup as cohomological obstruction

Blowup as obstruction. At q = 1, the spectral decay is polynomial: |\hat{v}_k(t)| \sim k^{-s} for some Sobolev exponent s. The obstruction class \kappa_n(v_1(t)) at level n depends on the n-th jet of v, which requires derivatives of order n. If v \in H^s with s finite, the n-th jet is undefined for n > s. The lifting fails:

  \kappa_n(v_1(t)) \neq 0
  \quad\text{for}\quad
  n > s(t),

where s(t) is the Sobolev regularity at time t.

Finite-time blowup means finite obstruction level. If a NS solution loses regularity at time T^*, its Sobolev exponent s(t) \to s^* as t \to T^{*-} for some finite s^* \geq 0. The obstruction level is:

  n^* = \lfloor s^* \rfloor + 1.

The velocity field ceases to lift at this level. The blowup localises here:

  • Below n^*: the velocity is smooth and lifts perfectly.
  • At n^*: the obstruction class \kappa_{n^*} is nonzero. The twisted 2-cocycle condition (descent condition) fails.
  • Above n^*: the solution does not exist in those gerbes.
